newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda resumes firing into Zaire - aid officials.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda resumes firing into Zaire - aid officials.

text.p: The Rwandan army has resumed machinegun and mortar fire over the border into eastern Zaire since Friday following a lull of several days, aid officials said.
But a Rwandan military spokesman denied the report.
"Since Friday the firing has been going on. Mortars and machine-guns have been used. The firing is 20 km (12 miles) north of Bukavu," an aid official in eastern Zaire told Reuters by telephone.
"On 29 September firing went onto (Zaire's) Birava island from Rwanda," he added, saying he had no reports of casualties.
"This is simply not correct. There has been no firing from the Rwandan side of the border. If there had been I would have known about it," said Major Emmanuel Ndahiro in the Rwandan capital.
Rwanda and Zaire exchanged fire across their border last week but there was a lull of several days in the fighting.

Zaire's relations with Rwanda have been poor since 1994 but worsened this month. An estimated 1.1 million Rwandan Hutu refugees live in eastern Zaire and the Rwandan government accuses Zaire of backing guerrilla incursions by Hutu rebels.
The U.N. High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR) evacuated about 15 staff last week from the border Zairean town of Bukavu because of the firing. Other aid staff were also pulled out.

"We have only seven staff in Bukavu since last week's events and those who were evacuated, some fifteen, are still in Goma (eastern Zaire) waiting to be redeployed depending on the security situation," said UNHCR spokesman Paul Stromberg.
The U.N. World Food Programme last week pulled out more than 50 foreign staff from Bukavu.
Zaire said on Saturday that infiltrators from Rwanda had killed at least 35 people and wounded three this month during cross-border attacks to destabilise its eastern refugee zone.
Government spokesman Oscar Lugendo, stepping up a war of words against Rwanda's government in Rwanda, said everything was being done to ensure the security of Zaireans living in South Kivu province.

The television showed footage of what it said were five Rwandan soldiers captured in Uvira near the border with Burundi. Zaire has accused Burundi, where the Tutsi-led army holds power, and aid groups of helping Rwandan infiltrators.
Human rights groups have accused Zairean soldiers of carrying out atrocities in South Kivu against Banyamulenge Tutsis, some of whom have lived in the area for generations.
